answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed on proven fraud, like a ferrous gate that only opens once a deposit is locked. New identities start in a quarantined garden where they may handle only small, supervised jobs until peers attest consistent work over time. An attacker wanting thousands of fakes must lock capital and wait through slow attestation for each one, and any karst-like hidden shortcut collapses because there is no cheap path around the stake and the waiting period: fraud costs the stake itself.
